handoff_contract_choices: panel.project(game_event, matches): stored GameEvent (store.put_event shape with period and scoringPlay) and P2-B04T matches {profileId, eventId, revision, starters, cursor}; recomputes PanelState for each matched profile; never writes Alerts.

panel.snapshot(profile_id, team_league) returns the CONTRACT-AFC-P2-ENVELOPE body: schemaVersion int, opaque id stable per profile and team/league, revision unchanged on re-read and strictly greater when content changes, source = active lineup source (yahoo | manual, as the frozen P2-B03T deployed tests already require), updatedAt RFC 3339 UTC.

data follows the P2-A05T TV wire shape (PanelFixtures.kt, typed gap PANEL_WIRE_UNFROZEN): teamLeague, scoringBasis (yahooLeague | ppr | halfPpr), rows [{playerId, name, points, gameStatus}], teamTotal, progress, value objects {value, reason, source, asOf}. This suite adds three keys the TV decoder ignores (it reads with opt()): stale (bool per value object), visible (Settings.panelPrefs.visible, default True) and games.

Statistics gap: the stored GameEvent carries no per-player statistics and store.put_event rejects extra attributes, so P2-B07 has no statistics source inside its write set. Seam panel.player_statistics(athlete_id) -> None or {gameId, gameState pre|in|post, gameStatus, source live|replay, asOf, stats {CONTRACT-AFC-P2-PRESETS stat name: number}}, read at call time through the panel module; tests replace it. Production may return None (every point unknown with a reason) until a slice stores ESPN boxscore statistics (same pattern as the P2-B06 event_channel seam).
Clock seam panel.now() -> RFC 3339 UTC string; staleness is evaluated at snapshot time from each value's source asOf, never from projection or response time.

stale_after boundary: age >= 60 s is stale (59 fresh, 60 and 61 stale), matching the P2-A05T TV decision and the register's '60 s'; design.md 'older than stale_after' is read the same way. A value with no asOf is stale.

team/league key is '<league>/<team>' of the Lineups row (the TV LineupPanel query; Settings.teamLeague is {league, team}). team_league None selects Settings.teamLeague, else the active lineup's pair. A pair other than the active lineup's returns no rows and an unknown total.

playerId is the ESPN athlete id; Yahoo starters map through matcher.PLAYER_MAP_PATH (exact name + team + position, as P2-B04T); an unmatched Yahoo starter keeps a row with unknown points and a reason.

teamTotal sums row points under the basis (asOf = oldest row asOf, stale when any row is stale); with any unknown row it is None or carries a non-empty reason. progress is pinned only at 0 (every game pre), 1 (every game post) and strictly between for a mix; the exact formula is the implementer's.

Manual points apply lineup.presets.TABLES by reference; a statistic without a table row awards no points (row unknown with a reason, or the statistic ignored). Yahoo points apply stat_modifiers; a statistic without a modifier scores nothing. A stored preset outside ppr/halfPpr is refused (exception) or every point is unknown.

games {gameId: {eventId, revision, score, source}} holds the projected event facts so the panel can be compared with the alert record (revision, triggerContext.score/source, P2-B05T shape). A later revision of the same eventId replaces them in place; an equal or lower revision never does. Replacement between different events of one game is only exercised for a later eventTime.

Settings changes (preset, team/league, visibility) are reflected on the next snapshot with a higher revision and no new event; a starter change is exercised as the Lineups change followed by the next projected event for that profile.
Points are compared with abs tolerance 0.005 so the implementer may round to two decimals.

No per-player statistics reach the store: GameEvent has only playerIds and store.put_event rejects other attributes, so the panel cannot compute points in production without a feed_ingest/store change (backend-template lease). The suite binds a player_statistics seam instead.

ApiFunction has Panels GetItem only, so GET /v1/panel cannot persist a read-time revision bump after a settings change; the revision must be derived (the scratch reference used projection counter + profile revision). Moto does not enforce IAM, so the unit suite cannot catch a PutItem from the API path.
